description_en: The Temple of Dattātreya, also known as the Candannātha Mandira, is situated at the heart of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār). This temple is a key component of an architectural complex consisting of two courtyards. The north courtyard houses the temple of Baṭuk Bhairab, also known as Bhairavnāth (JUM0291), at its center. Access to the temple complex is through this northern courtyard. A corridor connects to the southern courtyard, where the temple of Dattātreya is centrally located. These two temples, the Dattātreya temple, and the Baṭuk Bhairab temple, are often collectively referred to as the Candannātha Mandira.The temple itself is positioned in the center of the south courtyard. It boasts a square layout constructed with stone masonry, and its facades are adorned in white and ochre. The primary entrance to the temple faces east but is generally kept closed. Another entrance can be found on the western side, and it's likely that doors were once present on the north and south sides, suggested by the walled-off sections on these sides of the structure. A gilded copper dome gracefully covers the roof.In front of the main door, there is a rectangular raised platform adorned with white tiles. On and around this platform, one can find various stone and metal statues, including two stone Nandi bulls, a śivaliṅga, and a Gaṇeśa (001) enshrined at ground level on a small altar. Additional stone statues of Gaṇeśa are placed at the northeast (002) and southeast (003) corners of the temple's platform.To the west of the temple stand three substantial wooden poles adorned with flags. Known as liṅga, these poles are said to measure 52 feet, symbolizing the 52 weeks in a year. They are replaced annually on the day of ghasthpana.The rooms in the wings surrounding the temple serve various purposes, including storage, ritual spaces, and accommodations for pilgrims. An entrance to the complex is located in the southeastern corner of the courtyard, passing by the office of the Śrī Candannatha, Bhairavnātha Guṭhī Samiti, the trust responsible for the temple's upkeep.Two inscriptions on large stone slabs are positioned along the wall of the northern wing of the courtyard. These inscriptions date back to 1908 CE (ŚS 1965) and 1878 CE (VS 1934) and document donations made to the temple.According to legend, the Nāth yogi Candannāth transformed the Jumla region, originally occupied by a lake, into arable land fit for agriculture. He carried with him a grain of rice from Kashmir, which he planted and taught the locals how to cultivate. This story unfolds during the rule of the Sijapati dynasty, synonymous with the Kalyāl dynasty. Some sources suggest that Chandannāth himself placed the first Kalyāl king, Bālirāja, on the throne (Shrestha 2010, p. 13), while others identify King Medinī Varmā. Both historical figures are documented in the late 14th and early 15th centuries. The myth of the Jumla lake's transformation into agricultural land by a revered figure mirrors similar narratives found in the Buddhist text of the Svayambhūpurāṇa, which describes the Kathmandu valley's history.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a pāṭī and an okhala
historical_events.event_description: An inscription dated of 1908 CE (ŚS 1965) installed along the wall of the north wing records the donation of apāṭīand anokhalaby one Vāsudeva Jyotirvid (astrologer) and his wife Aṃvikā.Reading of the inscription by Rajendra Shakya:स्वस्तिश्री शाके १८३० श्रीसंवत् १९६५ साल कार्तिक शुदि ११ वुधवाररे कार्तिक २० गतेमा गोर्षा लुइटेल वस्ने लेफटें वासुदेव ज्योतिर्विद्... ... ... ... ... अंविका देकं तस्य तृतिय जात दिट्ठा देविभगत ज्योतिर्विद् ...... ... तस्य वागांगि भार्ज्यायां पुर्णकुमारि देव्यांतत्पुत्रलेफटें भुमिनंदनं १ पुन्यराज १ लिलावल्लभ १ कालिकाप्रसाद १ पुत्रियां मनोरमा १ कृष्णमाया १ नर्मदा १ रत्नकुमारी १ पौत्रायां दामोदर शहित सकल परिवाराःयां आयुरारोग्य सांत्यर्थं इहलोके सुखप्राप्ती परलोकेःमोक्ष प्राप्ती कामनया श्री गुरु महाराज चंदंनाथ स्वामि प्रशन प्राप्ती कामनार्थं यहमकान श्री चंदंनाथ स्वामि पृतय समर्पंयामि गोगृहप्रलोकशुधारणानिमित्त डिट्ठा देविभक्त डिट्ठेनि पुर्णकुमारिले श्री परमेश्वर प्रीति गरि चढायाको जस्ले भत्काइ विगारि देला तेसलाइ माहापातक लागि कुहिहेला फकिर फकेडा वाहेक दुनिञाले यो पाटिमा रहनाको मन गया श्री गुरुकी संवार तोतलाई ... ...को घ्यू धार्नि ६ पठाइ भत्के विग्रेको वनाउनु पुण्य होलापुजाहारि भंडारी कोठारिले पजनी गर्दा सो पाटी वीग्य्रानन परमेस्वरले सजाय गरुं भनि पाटि र वषलस्मेत चढाञ्यू सो दत्तपरदत्त वा नोहरोच वसुंधरा सद्धी वर्ष सहा... णि विष्ठायाजायत्तकमि ॥ १ ॥Synopsis:On Wednesday, the 11th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika in 1908 CE (ŚS 1965), Lieutenant Vāsudeva Jyotirvid (astrologer) and [his wife] Aṃvikā, along with their family, from the Luiṭela of Gorkha offered a pāṭī along with an okhala (stone mortar) in the name of venerable guru Mahārāja Candananātha.

Synopsis of the inscription:On Thursday, the 5th of the bright fortnight of Māgha in 1878 CE (VS 1934), Harkadeva Upādhyā made a certain donation in the name of venerable Candananātha of Dīpāyalagāũ of Jumlā.
